summary: Preinstall script downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that runs automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs checks whether `bun` is on PATH and, if not, downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from GitHub releases (`https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/...zip`), extracts it to a temp directory, chmod +x's the binary, and then invokes it via `execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')], {stdio:'inherit'})`. The sibling `math_init.js` is a 727 KB heavily obfuscated file carrying a `// @bun @bun-cjs` header, hex-named identifiers (`_0x...`), and a rotated string-array dispatch — a classic string-array obfuscator payload. Execution occurs exclusively under the freshly-downloaded Bun runtime, so the payload bypasses Node-based inspection. Neither `setup.mjs` nor `math_init.js` is declared in the package.json `files` array (which lists only `lib` and `index.d.ts`), and neither is referenced by the datepicker library code itself — `lib/index.js` is a legitimate fork of Kiarash-Z/react-modern-calendar-datepicker and acts as a decoy around the added install-time dropper. A React datepicker library has no legitimate reason to fetch a second language runtime and execute a large obfuscated sibling script at install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
